name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,537

clue.text: Sweet desert dweller inspiring artist

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the desert animal takes the artist inside itself

blocks.note: the animal of the desert
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A desert nomad with a sweet tooth gives an artist inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: A caramel is a chewy toffee, so it names a kind of sweet or confection.

clue.text: Argue puzzles must include smut (just a bit)?

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the puzzles enclose the extra letter
only a tiny bit of the word is wanted, namely its opening letter

blocks.note: grid puzzles like this one
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Crossword setters are told to slip in a little smut.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for disputing or quarrelling, from the image of duelling.

clue.text: Odour more horrible, rank ultimately? That is right

blocks.note: a reek is a strong unpleasant smell
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A smell gets worse and worse until it is truly rank, and someone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: something that ends up rank, more horribly so, smells worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Smellier, stinking worse, is what rank comes to mean when something gets more offensive in odour.

clue.text: Controversial 1950s US Senator’s match - cry off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of kilter, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A notorious senator calls off a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph McCarthy led the 1950s anti-communist witch hunts in the US Senate and was widely condemned.

clue.text: Makes connection between sexual deviations after leader’s replaced

indicators.note: replaced says that the first letter of the deviations is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: kinks are unusual sexual preferences
the word leader supplies its own initial letter

explanation.surface: Someone draws a link between sexual habits once the boss is replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading K of the deviations is swapped for the L at the front of leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To link things is to join or connect them, so this verb means makes connection between.

clue.text: Blogger Bill

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who puts messages up online
second meaning: a printed notice stuck on a wall

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words look like a person called Bill who writes a blog; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who posts online content is one sense; a bill pasted up for advertising is a printed notice of the same name.

clue.text: Very amusing, invaluable

blocks.note: first meaning: hilarious, informally
second meaning: worth more than any sum of money

explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means hilarious, and literally it means too precious to put a cost on.

clue.text: Rest as site out of order

indicators.note: out of order means not in the proper sequence, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Work stops for a break because the site is out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short rest taken in hot countries.

clue.text: Charm of French anthem

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters come out of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: The charm of the Marseillaise.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in plain sight across the end of French and the start of anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to cast a spell over or delight, which is what to charm means as a verb.

clue.text: Being cocky about scam I’d introduced to dishonest person

indicators.note: what is introduced to something is put inside it, so the short phrase goes into the crook

blocks.note: over can mean about, as in a row over money
a con is a swindle
a fence is a dealer in stolen goods
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A swaggering conman is caught out after slipping his scam to a crooked partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cocky means having too much self-belief, which is excessive certainty about one's own abilities.

clue.text: Unexpected risk limits English winter sportsman

indicators.note: something unexpected turns out differently from how it looked, so the letters are rearranged
to limit is to set bounds around, so the reworked letters enclose the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English athlete on the slopes faces an unforeseen hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes downhill on skis takes part in a snow sport, so is a winter sportsman.

clue.text: Points at musicians’ headgear

blocks.note: three compass points: south, west, east
taken as written
a group of musicians playing together

explanation.surface: Someone gestures at the hats the band members are wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatband is a strip of fabric worn round the forehead, so it counts loosely as headgear.

clue.text: Players’ local game - like some cricket?

blocks.note: a derby is a match between two local rivals
county cricket is the English first-class domestic game

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood match that resembles a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: DERBY COUNTY is an English football club, so its players make up the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club's team is its players, so the club name stands for the squad on the pitch.

clue.text: Perhaps one involved in service dispute over exporter?

indicators.note: in a down-style reading, over means turned back, so the quarrel word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a row is a quarrel
someone who sends goods abroad ships them

explanation.surface: A disagreement at a tennis match or with an export firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests tennis or business, but the definition means a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchgoer at a religious service is someone who prays and venerates God, an example of such a participant.

clue.text: I've gripe possibly about introduction of lawyer’s immunity claim?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so the reworked letters surround the selected one
an introduction is the start, so only the first letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grumbling client complains about a lawyer claiming immunity.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal privilege is an exemption that lets someone refuse disclosure, a right asserted as protection from liability.

clue.text: Big name instrument one’s lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is taken out of the instrument

blocks.note: the long-necked Indian stringed instrument
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrity musician has mislaid an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous celebrity, and a celebrity performer is commonly called this.

clue.text: City loan term renegotiated

indicators.note: something renegotiated has its terms rearranged, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A city's borrowing terms are reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreal is the largest city in the Canadian province of Quebec.

clue.text: Girl was in revolt

blocks.note: first meaning: a woman's first name
second meaning: past tense of the verb for rebelling

explanation.surface: A girl who rebelled.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female forename, and the past tense of the verb meaning to rise in rebellion.

clue.text: Worth seeing Presley regularly after Quiet American’s Number One

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the singer's name is kept
number one is the first in line, so only the initial letter of the nationality is kept

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
the first letter of the word
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Elvis is worth watching, coming after a quiet American hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quiet American is a Graham Greene novel, and Elvis had many number ones; both are surface distractions.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapely means attractively formed, so a shapely figure is pleasant to look at.

clue.text: Such a position for the other girl with island line

definitions.text: Such a position for the other

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman
Iona is a small Scottish island in the Inner Hebrides
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about bedroom arrangements involving another girl on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British slang for sex, so the definition points at the familiar position name.
explanation.definitionFit: The missionary position is the standard face-to-face sexual position, named humorously after Christian missionaries.

clue.text: Move up from here

blocks.note: surface reading: advice to gain promotion from your current place
setter's reading: the place where planes leave the ground and climb into the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Move up' sounds like career progress, but it is literal: aircraft rise from the runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Flights take off from an aerodrome, so it is where passengers literally go upward into the air.

clue.text: Act like a foolish person? Go away!

blocks.note: to be something is to act as it
taken as written
tit is British slang for an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop behaving stupidly and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command telling someone to leave at once, like clear off.

clue.text: Feature of your day just now perhaps - cut in items at sea?

definitions.text: Feature of your day just now perhaps

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and disordered, so these letters are jumbled
in tells us the word for trimming goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: to pare is to trim or cut
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cutting items while on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition addresses the solver directly: doing a crossword is presumably what you do when free.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure hours are a part of most people's day, and solving puzzles right now is probably using them.

clue.text: Instruction redraft safeguards clubs

indicators.note: to safeguard something is to keep it protected inside, so the card suit sits within

blocks.note: to edit is to revise a text
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A revised directive protects golf or social clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or order issued by an authority, a formal command.

clue.text: Body temperature, approximately

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
or so means roughly, as in ten minutes or so

explanation.surface: A rough reading of someone's body temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human frame, sometimes simply called the body apart from limbs and head.

clue.text: Disappoint 11?

blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to let down whatever is at 11 in the grid
setter's reading: 11 is the size of a football or cricket team, so failing your eleven teammates

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the football club at 11 down, but the number itself also means a team of eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing one's teammates is the idiom for disappointing those who relied on you.

clue.text: On return in hotel, try menu girl’s seen

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read right to left
in says the answer is sitting inside the following run of words

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of hotel, all of try and the start of menu

explanation.surface: Back at the hotel, a girl is spotted sampling the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, borrowed from the evergreen shrub with fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Writer’s opening rebuffed by flirt

indicators.note: a rebuff pushes something back, so the gap word is read backwards

blocks.note: a slot is a narrow opening
to toy with someone is to flirt with them

explanation.surface: An author's advances are rejected by a coquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy, the Russian novelist of War and Peace, is a famous author.
